entities.summary: The Asiatic Society of Mumbai is a learned society in the field of Asian studies based in Mumbai, India. It can trace its origin to the Literary Society of Bombay which first met in Mumbai on 26 November 1804, and was founded by Sir James Mackintosh. It was formed with the intention of "promoting useful knowledge, particularly such as is now immediately connected with India". After the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland was established in London in 1823, the Literary Society of Bombay became affiliated with it and was known as the Bombay Branch of the Royal Asiatic Society (BBRAS) since 1830.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Asiatic Society of Mumbai played a crucial role in promoting Asian studies and facilitating cultural exchange between India and Europe. Its affiliation with the Royal Asiatic Society helped establish Bombay as a major center for Oriental learning, shaping the trajectory of Indian scholarship.
